newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Nera announces flourish of deals.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Nera announces flourish of deals.

text.p: Norwegian telecommunications company Nera ASA said on Thursday it had won a contract with Korea Telecom for a satellite earth station, bringing the total value of deals announced this week to 160 million crowns.
The international company said the station, worth between 20 and 30 million crowns, would provide services for the Inmarsat system. It is due to be ready by the fourth quarter.
Earlier this week Nera announced a 100 million crown deal with state Norwegian telecom group Telenor, for the delivery of equipment and services to GrameenPhone in Bangladesh.
The company also signed a 40 million crown package with Botswana Telecom for deliveries and services for developing a high-capacity radio link connecting the Botswana telecom network to Namibia.
Nera spokesman Helge Skaar said the deals proved the company's commitment to international markets.
"The Bangladesh contract is a completely new market for us and it will also be interesting to work internationally with Telenor," Skaar said.
"We have been in Botswana for many years, and the Korean contract will help develop Mini-M terminals in Asia."
At 1435 GMT Nera's share price was up 14.50 crowns at 335.00 crowns in thin trade.
